# embedded-build-tools

Source: https://github.com/hxyulin/embedded-build-tools/blob/main/README.md

# embedded-build-tools

Reusable building blocks for **bare-metal Rust kernel build pipelines** —
the parts Cargo and the wider ecosystem don't cover out of the box,
packaged as a library you drive from a [`cargo xtask`][xtask] rather than
from a bespoke build system.

```toml
[dependencies]
embedded-build-tools = { version = "0.1", features = ["image", "qemu", "cargobuild"] }
```

## Philosophy

Modern bare-metal Rust is well served by Cargo plus a few nightly
features:

- **Sysroots** → `-Z build-std`
- **Two-triple bootloader/kernel handoff** → `-Z bindeps` (artifact
  dependencies)
- **Per-crate linker scripts / cfgs** → a crate's own `build.rs`
- **Running in QEMU** → the `runner` key in `.cargo/config.toml`

What's left over is glue: assembling a bootable disk image, launching
QEMU with the right firmware, Kconfig-style options. That glue has to
live *somewhere* — but it doesn't need a whole build system wrapped
around it. `embedded-build-tools` is that glue as a plain library, so
your build orchestration can stay an ordinary `cargo xtask`.

Every tool is a **primitive**: given an explicit spec and an output path,
do one well-defined thing and report what happened. There is no build
graph, no cache, and no config-file format baked in — those belong to the
caller.

## Tools

Each sits behind a cargo feature so you only compile what you use.

| Feature | Status | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | ✅ available | Assemble bootable disk images: flat FAT32 and MBR-partitioned disks (ESP, raw boot-sector writes, auto-sizing). |
| `qemu` | ✅ available | Build a QEMU command line, discover OVMF firmware, and launch the guest with a timeout and Ctrl-C teardown. |
| `cargobuild` | ✅ available | Drive `cargo`, resolve the real artifact paths it produces from the JSON message stream, and convert ELF → flat binary with objcopy. |
| `kconfig` | 🚧 planned | Kconfig-style typed configuration options (ranges, dependencies, presets). |

## Example: assemble an ESP

```rust
use std::path::PathBuf;
use embedded_build_tools::image::{
    DiskImage, EntrySource, FileEntry, FsType, Layout,
};

let image = DiskImage {
    name: "boot".into(),
    size_mb: None, // auto-size, 64 MiB floor
    layout: Layout::Flat {
        fs_type: FsType::Fat32,
        entries: vec![FileEntry {
            dest_path: "/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI".into(),
            source: EntrySource::File { path: PathBuf::from("target/bootloader.efi") },
        }],
    },
};

let report = embedded_build_tools::image::build(&image, "disk.img".as_ref())?;
print!("{}", report.log);
# Ok::<(), embedded_build_tools::Error>(())
```

For a hybrid BIOS+UEFI disk, use `Layout::Partitioned` with an MBR table,
an ESP partition, and a `RawWrite` supplying the boot sector at LBA 0.

## Example: boot a kernel under QEMU

```rust
use std::path::PathBuf;
use embedded_build_tools::qemu::{self, Boot, PathCheck, QemuConfig};

// Pick a binary from the target triple, or set one explicitly.
let binary = qemu::default_binary_for_target("x86_64-unknown-none")?;

let mut config = QemuConfig::new(binary, Boot::Direct {
    kernel: PathBuf::from("target/x86_64-unknown-none/debug/my-kernel"),
});
config.memory_mb = 512;
config.timeout = Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30)); // for CI

let command = qemu::build_command(&config, PathCheck::Skip)?; // Skip: dry-run
println!("{}", command.to_shell());   // dry-run: print the argv
// let status = command.spawn_and_wait()?;   // or actually launch it
# Ok::<(), embedded_build_tools::Error>(())
```

For UEFI, discover firmware with `qemu::discover_ovmf(...)` and pass the
resulting `Ovmf` into `Boot::Uefi { ovmf, drive }`.

## Example: build a kernel and resolve its artifact

Cargo builds bare-metal crates fine — what it won't tell you is *where*
the output landed (the path has a content hash you can't predict). Ask
it, by reading the JSON message stream:

```rust
use embedded_build_tools::cargobuild::{self, CargoBuild, Profile};

let spec = CargoBuild {
    package: Some("my-kernel".into()),
    target: Some("x86_64-unknown-none".into()),
    profile: Profile::Release,
    ..CargoBuild::new()
};

let output = cargobuild::run(&spec)?;        // spawns cargo, parses artifacts
let kernel = output.executable()?;           // the real, on-disk path

// …which drops straight into the QEMU primitive:
// QemuConfig::new(binary, Boot::Direct { kernel: kernel.to_path_buf() })
# Ok::<(), embedded_build_tools::Error>(())
```

This is the seam the three features share: `cargobuild` resolves the
path, `image` stages it onto a disk (or `qemu` boots it directly). For a
bare-metal integration test, use `Subcommand::TestNoRun` — its
`executable` is the test harness binary you boot under QEMU with an
`isa-debug-exit` device. The sysroot itself still comes from `-Z
build-std` in `.cargo/config.toml`; `cargobuild` runs the build, it
doesn't replace Cargo.

## Runnable example

[`examples/hello-boot`](examples/hello-boot) is a complete `cargo xtask`
project that boots a "hello world" two ways, wiring all three features
together:

```sh
cd examples/hello-boot
cargo xtask uefi              # cargobuild → image → qemu: a UEFI app on an ESP, booted by OVMF
cargo xtask bios              # image → qemu: a NASM boot sector on an MBR disk, booted by SeaBIOS
cargo xtask uefi --dry-run    # build + assemble, then print the QEMU argv instead of launching
```

It doubles as a template for adapting the primitives to a real kernel —
see its [README](examples/hello-boot/README.md).

## Provenance

These tools were extracted from [Gluon][gluon], a from-scratch bare-metal
build system, once `-Z build-std` and `-Z bindeps` matured enough that a
full rustc-driving build system was no longer worth maintaining. The
image, QEMU, artifact-resolution, and Kconfig subsystems were the parts
that pulled their weight independently of the build graph — so they live
on here as composable libraries. (`cargobuild` keeps only the half of
Gluon's build-std work that Cargo still doesn't do for you: parsing the
artifact stream to learn where outputs landed.)

# embedded-build-tools

Source: https://github.com/hxyulin/embedded-build-tools/blob/main/CLAUDE.md

# embedded-build-tools

## Overview

`embedded-build-tools` is a library of building blocks for bare-metal
Rust kernel build pipelines: bootable disk-image assembly (FAT32/ESP/MBR),
QEMU launching, Kconfig-style options, and `build-std`/metadata helpers.

It is **not** a build system. The expected consumer is a `cargo xtask`
(or a `build.rs`) that owns scheduling, incrementality, and configuration,
and calls into these tools for the specific jobs Cargo doesn't do. Each
tool is a primitive: given an explicit spec and an output path, do one
well-defined thing and report what happened — no build graph, no cache,
no config-file format baked in.

It is a host-side userland library, so it has no `no_std` or
zero-dependency constraints; mature crates (`hadris-fat`, `walkdir`,
`thiserror`, `serde`) are used where they pull their weight.

This crate was harvested from [Gluon](https://github.com/hxyulin/gluon),
a from-scratch build system, after `-Z build-std` and `-Z bindeps`
matured enough that the full build system was no longer worth
maintaining.

## Collaboration Instructions

1. **Always ask for clarification rather than assuming intent.** If a
   request is vague, ambiguous, or appears incorrect, stop and ask
   before acting.
2. **Consider multiple approaches.** Surface better options if they
   exist — explain the trade-offs rather than silently picking one.
3. **Be educational.** Offer brief explanations of *why* an approach is
   preferred, especially around on-disk formats and toolchain quirks.
4. **Plan before you build.** Discuss design, edge cases, and integration
   points before writing code.

## Engineering Guidelines

1. **Stay a library of primitives.** Resist growing a build graph, a
   cache, or a config format inside these tools — that belongs to the
   consuming xtask. Each entry point takes an explicit spec and a path.
2. **Stay kernel-agnostic.** No assumptions about a specific kernel,
   bootloader, or boot protocol. The caller supplies concrete paths and
   bytes.
3. **Feature-gate every tool.** A consumer that only assembles images
   must not compile the QEMU launcher. Shared pieces (the error type)
   stay unconditional and small.
4. **Determinism first.** Identical inputs must produce byte-identical
   outputs: stable iteration order (sort directory walks), no reliance
   on filesystem ordering or `HashMap` iteration.
5. **Minimize `unsafe`.** This is a host tool; `unsafe` is forbidden at
   the crate root (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). Keep it that way.
6. **Surface errors with context.** Every error names the offending
   image, partition, entry, or path. Anonymous errors are bugs.
7. **Document intent, not mechanics.** Comments explain *why* — on-disk
   layout choices, the FAT label trick, the LBA-vs-byte boundary —
   where the "what" is obvious but the "why" is not.

## Testing

- `cargo test --features image` — unit + end-to-end image tests (real
  FAT32 formatting and MBR stamping against temp files).
- `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` — must be clean.
- Byte-level assertions for deterministic structures (MBR); structural
  assertions (size, signature, progress log) for FAT contents.

# Contributing

Source: https://github.com/hxyulin/embedded-build-tools/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in `embedded-build-tools`.

## Ground rules

- **It's a library of primitives, not a build system.** New code takes an
  explicit spec and an output path, does one job, and reports what
  happened. If a change wants a build graph, a cache, or a config-file
  format, that logic belongs in the consuming `xtask`, not here.
- **Feature-gate new tools.** A new subsystem (e.g. `gpt`, `ext4`) goes
  behind its own cargo feature so consumers compile only what they use.
- **Determinism is a hard requirement.** Identical inputs must produce
  byte-identical outputs. Sort directory walks; never depend on
  filesystem or `HashMap` iteration order.
- **Errors must name the offender.** Every error points at a specific
  image, partition, entry, or path.
- **`unsafe` is forbidden** at the crate root. Keep it that way.

## Before you open a PR

```sh
cargo test --all-features
cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets   # must be clean
cargo fmt --all
```

Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` describing the change.

## Commit messages

Conventional-commit style (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`)
with a scope where it helps (`feat(image): GPT partition tables`).
